name: Ish-Bosheth
bio:
Ish-Bosheth was a son of Saul. After Saul and Jonathan died at Mount Gilboa, Abner, commander of Saul's army, made Ish-Bosheth king over Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin, and the rest of Israel; he was forty years old and reigned two years, while David ruled only over the tribe of Judah, and a long war followed between the two houses (2 Samuel 2:8-11; 3:1).

Ish-Bosheth once confronted Abner over sleeping with his father's concubine Rizpah; Abner grew furious at the accusation and threatened to hand the kingdom over to David entirely, and Ish-Bosheth, afraid of him, could not answer a word (2 Samuel 3:7-11). Abner indeed turned to support David soon after, but was assassinated by Joab on his way to seal the alliance, leaving Ish-Bosheth and all Israel disheartened and alarmed (2 Samuel 4:1).

Two of Ish-Bosheth's military officers, Baanah and Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Benjamite, sneaked into his house while he lay resting at noon, struck him down, and cut off his head, bringing it to David at Hebron expecting a reward. David instead rebuked them for murdering an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed, and had them executed, burying Ish-Bosheth's head in Abner's tomb at Hebron (2 Samuel 4:5-12). Ish-Bosheth's death marked the end of the long war between the house of Saul and the house of David, clearing the final obstacle to David's rule over a united Israel.
